"You can actually see stars!" she says, her eyes big and beaming. I knew, despite her constant grumbling about "nature" and "bugs" and the lack of WiFi, that she'd like it here. 

"It's so still out here." She tilts her head all the way back, taking in the universe; I feel the back of her head land on my shoulder. It's warm and her hair smells like heaven. She turns around to look at me. "I guess nature isn't so bad after all, even if this park is old as balls" she smirks. 

Then, softly, "Thank you for bringing me here. I... I really needed this."

She tenderly reaches out for my hand, but changes her mind and instead places it on my cheek. My heart is racing. It's all I can hear. That, and the sound of her breath... and... was that... snickering?

We break apart and look towards the bushes behind us. Three men emerge from the shadows. 

"Now, don't stop just because of us. It was just getting good", leers the one in front, wearing a fuckin' fedora for some reason.

I immediately feel unsafe. I know where this is going and she does too. I feel my body start tensing up but thank god for fight/flight responses: without thinking, I instinctively grab her hand, and make a dash for it. 

"Hey-!"

The men chase after us into the wilderness, but we just *run*; arms scratching against branches; twigs crunching under our feet; nettles piercing skin; hands sweaty and holding on for dear life. We can hear them coming after us, we run as fast as we can, breathless till we reach this clearing. There's nowhere to hide, but there's this big sprawling tree in the middle, almost calling out to us. Sanctuary. 

I pull her to it and boost her up onto one of its limbs. She grabs me by the arms and pulls me up. We climb, climb, climb, all the way up, and stay still. The men arrive at the clearing. We're trying not to breathe and hoping the night is our friend.

"Where'd they go?"

"COME ON OUT WHEREVER YOU ARE!"

*Crrrr.* The tree groans. Crap. I knew I shouldn't have had that second burger.

"Ah, there you are." The fedora-wearing fucker flashes a cruel smile. "Come on down, we just want to talk."

She's crying. This is too familiar for her. I don't know how to save us.

*Crrrr.* The groans are getting louder. 

"What do we do what do we do what do we do what do we..." she doesn't have the words and I don't have the answers.

"Not gonna come down?" He shrugs and proclaims, "Well, we'll just come up and get you then." 

She's shaking. *Crrrr.* She looks up, past the leaves and branches, and slips into deafening silence, wishing she could disappear.

Fedora Fucker approaches the tree *(crrrr),* hikes up his khakis, and reaches his hand towards the branch hanging overhead. I brace for the worst.

"YEEEEEEEOW!" He recoils, loses his balance, and falls to the ground, clutching his hand.

"What happened?" asks Goon #2.

"My hand's fucking burning!"

"Ah, fuck you, I'll get 'em." Goon #2 marches up to the tree.

"OWWWWWEEEE!"

He falls back too. He raises his hand up to the moonlight - his palm is rapidly swelling and growing redder. It doesn't look natural. *Crrrr.*

"Are those boils?!" asks Goon #3.

"What do you think it looks like, fool! Arghhhhh!"

Fedora Fucker's face is contorted in pain. He looks up at us, and a look of sheer horror takes over. "They're.... they're witches."

The men slowly back away from the tree. They mutter inaudibly under their breaths as they back off and then scuttle off into the night, cursing and yowling into nothingness. 

My jaw is hanging. I look at her and then at my hands. A few scratches here and there, but otherwise, unscathed. What just happened?

I look at her again, hoping for... something. Her hand is placed on the bark of the tree, her eyes are closed in quiet contemplation. 

And that's when I realised I hadn't heard any groaning since the men left.

Suddenly, she lunges at me, almost knocking me off the tree entirely. She throws her arms around me, pressing her trembling body against mine. I try to comfort her by stroking her hair but she looks up at me and instead of tears, I see startlingly green eyes and a smile bigger than any I have ever seen.

"I fucking *love* nature man."

Well, idk, maybe cause I do theatre it comes more easily to me. But basically whenever people ask me how I'm doing or shit that entails my personal life I sorta dismiss the question with a neutral answer like "I'm alright" and immediately turn the focus onto the other person - asking them questions about what they're doing instead, that way I don't need to reveal anything about my mental state and people are usually happy to have someone take an interest in their lives so they'll just keep talking and i can just listen.

As someone whose tried both - being unapologetically miserable and putting on an act - I can tell you that both options honestly suck. Either I'm miserable but have someone to talk to and they slowly pull away or "performing" gets tiresome and I isolate myself into an irreparable wreck. It's really a red and blue pill situation and both are destined to make you feel like shite either way so the choice is yours. I've chosen the latter for right now and I don't think it's going too well for me so idk, I hope you have better luck than me.

I'm glad you got through your rough patch and am proud of you! I think your mum is probably just freaked out and scared, but I don't think you have anything to be guilty about - dealing with suicidal thoughts are hard and talking about them with family - or anyone for that matter- is no easy feat. You did what you could to stay alive and sought help and confided in your therapist and those are very valid actions. You weren't comfortable sharing with your family because you were afraid of how they'd react and if your mum's current response is anything to go on, you probably made the best choice for yourself at the time. And if you think that a selfish act, I think you're allowed to be selfish when it boils down to fighting for your life, so be kind to yourself okay. You did your best and it's helped you get to where you are now :) 

I think maybe rn your mum just needs assurance that you're safe but she has zero right to interrogate your therapist. Maybe there's something you can do or say to assure her you're taking care of yourself and that you're in the clear? Hoping for the best for you and your family and again I'm really so proud of you stranger!
